messages:
maria: Prod canary alert — error rate on model-serving v2 jumped to 12% over the last 2m. Noted increase in 95p latency too. Pager fired. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager (P1) triggered for service=model-serving, env=prod-canary, metric=5xx_rate, value=0.12, threshold=0.03. Incident channel created.
oncall-jordan: I'm oncall, I'm taking this. Thanks for the callout @maria. First step: limit traffic to canary and prep to flip flag if we confirm regression.
devon: looking at logs now — getting OOM-ish traces from the runtime when sequence length spikes, seems to correlate with a new kernel selection in the v2 build.
samir: can we pin to previous model variant quickly? We have a feature-flag controlling routing: `routes.model-serving:stable|canary`.
oncall-jordan: yes. I'm going to perform a soft kill-switch: route 100% to stable, keep canary isolated. Devon, if you have the rollback artifact ready, prep the canary evict.
devon: artifact ready. Command prepared: ```
# route traffic back to stable
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags/switch -d '{"flag":"routes.model-serving","value":"stable"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```
leo: pushing the route-flip now (runbook step 1).
incident-bot: Action log: route flip initiated by leo at 5349991182.
leo: done. Observability: 5xx dropping from 12% -> 1.8% in 45s, p95 latency improving. :white_check_mark:
cs-tilly: We have 4 tickets opened by customers; two are production errors impacting request flows. Notifying affected accounts with a rollback note.
oncall-jordan: great. Next: drain canary instances, hold deployments, run smoke-checks against stable. Devon/Samir — coordinate the drain and ensure KV cache warmup on stable.
devon: starting drain commands, will not terminate until in-flight tokens < 1%. Command run: `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deploy/model-serving-canary` then `drain-wait --threshold 1%`.
samir: also toggled autoscaler to avoid spinning new canary pods accidentally.
maria: monitoring synthesis tests — generating 50 synthetic requests to the typical long-tail sequences, stable handles them fine.
oncall-jordan: status update: customer impact contained, traffic routed to stable, errors trending to baseline. I'm marking mitigation in progress. Need verification from CS and Dev.
cs-tilly: sending customer update now: short note + ETA for postmortem.
leo: I've captured diagnostics from the canary nodes, uploading to the incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/5349991112/diagnostics.tar.gz
incident-bot: Evidence uploaded: diagnostics.tar.gz (leo). Runbook note: schedule postmortem with dev + oncall within 48h.
oncall-jordan: closing the live mitigation — continuing to monitor for 30m. If stable is healthy, we'll follow up with a rollback vs patch decision. For now, traffic back to stable.
maria: thanks all — saved a customer-impactful rollout. Please add any followups (kernel selection, sequence-length defensives, canary limits) to the incident doc.
devon: put an immediate guard: add sequence-length histogram alert to avoid future silent OOMs.
samir: creating a short checklist for next deploy: incremental kernel switch + small-percentage canaries + perf test with long sequences.
oncall-jordan: incident resolved (live). Will file the incident ticket: INC-5349991112 and assign owners. Postmortem required. :pencil:
cs-tilly: confirmed customers notified. Awaiting postmortem notes.
leo: final note — no data exfil, no config leak, just runtime mismatch.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Tagged: rollback-candidate, postmortem-required.
